title: Punctuating Titles of Works
keyIdea: When you write the name of a book, film, song or poem, the title needs a style so the reader knows it is a title. A whole work that stands alone (a book, film, album, newspaper, magazine or TV series) goes in italics when typed, or is underlined by hand. A part that sits inside a bigger work (a poem, short story, song, chapter, article or episode) goes in quotation marks. The first word, the last word and the main words of a title take capital letters; little words in the middle such as the, and, of and in stay small. Use the same style every time the title comes up.
familyTip: Look at the shelf or the playlist together. Ask: is this a whole thing, or one part of something bigger? The album is whole, so italics; each song on it is a part, so quotation marks. When your child writes by hand, check they underline book and film titles, and that Cat and Hat get capitals in The Cat in the Hat but in and the do not.

visual.caption: Italics (or underline by hand), or quotation marks? Drag each card, or tap it and then tap a box.

lab.caption: Flagship lab: sort whole works from parts, italics or underlining, title capitals, style each title in a sentence, and find the slips.

kid: A title is the name of a book, a film, a song or a poem. We mark it so the reader can see it is a name. Ask: is it a whole thing, or a part of a thing? A book is whole. A film is whole. An album of songs is whole. Type a whole thing in italics, like this: Frozen, in slanted letters.
A song is one part of an album. A poem is one part of a book of poems. A chapter is one part of a book. Put a part in quotation marks: "Let It Go".
You can not write slanted letters with a pen. So by hand, draw a line under a whole thing. A part still gets quotation marks.
Big words in a title get a capital. Small words in the middle, like the, and, of and in, stay small. The first word and the last word always get one.
adult: Ages 10 to 11. This is Common Core L.5.2d: use underlining, quotation marks, or italics to show titles of works. The usual rule is whole versus part. A whole work stands on its own: a book, film, album, play, newspaper, magazine, TV series or game. Its title goes in italics when typed. A part sits inside a larger work: a poem, short story, song, chapter, article or episode. Its title goes in quotation marks.

Underlining is the handwritten stand-in for italics. So a child writing by hand underlines what they would put in italics when typing. Parts keep their quotation marks either way. Some UK schools and papers put every title in inverted commas instead. Any house style is fine if it is used the same way each time, but the whole-versus-part rule is the one most style guides and US standards follow.

Title case: give capitals to the first word, the last word and all main words (nouns, pronouns, verbs, adjectives and adverbs). Keep a, an, the, short joining words and short place words small in the middle: The Lion, the Witch and the Wardrobe. In Where the Wild Things Are, Are is a verb, so it takes a capital.

Common mistakes: choosing by how famous or long the work feels, not by whole or part; putting book titles in quotation marks because speech uses them; dropping the style on the second mention; giving every word a capital, even in and the; and treating a short verb such as is or are as a little word. In the lab your child sorts 8 titles, styles typed and handwritten sentences, fixes 3 titles' capitals, styles 6 titles in sentences and finds 3 slips in a review.

practice.prompt: How should the book title look when you type it? I read Holes in two days.
practice.hint: Is a book a whole thing or a part of something?
practice.explain: A book is a whole work, so its title goes in italics when typed, or is underlined by hand.

practice.prompt: A list names {b} books and {s} songs. How many of the titles go in italics?
practice.hint: Only whole works go in italics. A song is one part of an album.
practice.explain: The {b} books are whole works, so they take italics. The {s} songs are parts, so they take quotation marks.

practice.prompt: Which title has the right capital letters?
practice.hint: Main words get capitals. Little words in the middle stay small.
practice.explain: James, Giant and Peach are main words. And and the are little words in the middle, so they stay small.

practice.prompt: A book has {c} chapters, and each chapter has a title. You write about the book and every chapter. How many titles go in quotation marks?
practice.hint: The book is the whole work. Each chapter is a part.
practice.explain: Each of the {c} chapters is a part, so {c} titles take quotation marks. The book title takes italics.

practice.prompt: You write by hand about the film Shrek. How do you show the title?
practice.hint: You can not write italics with a pen.
practice.explain: A film is a whole work. By hand, underlining stands in for italics.

choices: a poem in a poetry book
pool.hint: Find the part, not the whole.
pool.explain: One poem is a part of the book, so it takes quotation marks. The book and the TV series are whole works.

pool.prompt: A newspaper has an article called Bees Return to City Parks. How should the article title look?
choices: Bees Return to City Parks in italics
pool.hint: An article is one part of a newspaper.
pool.explain: An article is a part, so it takes quotation marks. The newspaper name would take italics.

pool.prompt: Which is the right reason to put a title in italics?
choices: It is a whole work that stands alone
pool.hint: Think about whole or part, not fame or size.
pool.explain: A famous song is still a part, and a short picture book is still whole. Whole or part decides.

pool.prompt: Which title has the right capitals?
pool.hint: Are is short, but what kind of word is it, and where is it?
pool.explain: Are is a verb and the last word, so it takes a capital. The in the middle stays small.

pool.prompt: An album has {n} songs. You write the album title and every song title. How many titles in all?
pool.hint: Count the songs, then add the album.
pool.explain: {n} song titles in quotation marks plus 1 album title in italics makes {=n+1} titles.

pool.prompt: A story says Wonder three times. The first time it is in italics. How should the next two look?
pool.hint: Same title, same style, every time it comes up.
pool.explain: Use the same style every time the title comes up, so Wonder stays in italics.

pool.prompt: A TV series and one episode of it. Which takes quotation marks?
pool.hint: Which one is a part of the other?
pool.explain: The episode is a part of the series, so it takes quotation marks. The series takes italics.

pool.prompt: A title has {w} words. Only the first word, the last word and {k} main words in between get capitals. How many words stay small?
pool.hint: Take away the first word, the last word and the main words.
pool.explain: {w} words minus 2 (first and last) minus {k} main words leaves {=w-2-k} little words in lower case.

pool.prompt: You write by hand about the poem Snow Day. How do you show it?
pool.hint: A poem is a part. Does handwriting change that?
pool.explain: A poem is a part, so it takes quotation marks whether typed or written by hand. Underlining is only for whole works.
